code-design.note: Every checked claim holds (help-toggle ordering, Line literal counts, make_state_with_lines, Ten source files) and the numbered call chains with per-step error paths and 18 listed assumptions make each decision pointable.

superpowers.note: Line references and the help-toggle ordering are verified and the versioned, read-only-aware store is thorough, but the lazy-flush justification cites a comment at markdown.rs:1101 that is about task markers (items actually flush at End(Item)), and the toast_warning/theme work is scope creep.

plain.note: Places the pending-key check inside handle_normal, so `m` then `h` or `?` is swallowed by is_help_toggle in handle_event first, and viewer-side units and signatures are only sketched in prose.

feature-dev.note: Correctly puts the pending intercept in handle_event and covers slide mode and the status prompt, but mixes a 1-based stored hint with a 0-based capture/resolve, relies on a stale-prone block_line stamp, and falls back to ~/.local/state on macOS.

reason: W is the only plan whose claims all check out against the code and which gives per-step call chains with explicit error paths and a numbered assumption list, so each decision can be challenged individually. X is nearly as strong but has a wrong justification for its stamping rule and adds unrelated toast/theme changes. Z has a line-indexing inconsistency and a fragile stamping scheme, and Y misses that help toggles are handled before handle_normal.
